newsitem.title: USA: Congoleum sees retail demand factor in '97 growth.
newsitem.headline: Congoleum sees retail demand factor in '97 growth.

text.p: Congoleum Corp said Thursday its its results for the balance of this year will depend largely on the strength of retail demand and the cost of PVC resins and other raw materials and other market factors.
"While I am hopeful we will see improvements in both these areas, our focus remains on positioning Congoleum for long-term success," said Roger Marcus, chairman of the flooring maker.

Marcus said reaction to Congoleum's new product, Designer Inlaid sheet vinyl, which begins shipping this month, has been "overwhelming." and that the company continues to expand market position in the do-it-yourself product category.

He said production line refurbishment at its Marcus Hook facility is proceeding ahead of schedule, and when completed this fall, should provide substantial improvements in efficiency and flexibility."
He issued the statement as the company released second quarter 1997 results. While the results were disappointing, he noted that they were consistent with expectations the company had in early June.
"Our second quarter suffered from an inability to promote sales while building inventory for an extended renovation shutdown, as well as a weak retail environment," he said.
The flooring maker said sales for the second quarter ended June 30, were $64.9 million, down 12.7 percent from $74.4 million in the second quarter of 1996.
Net earnings for the quarter were $2.1 million versus $4.8 million in 1996 producing earnings per share of $0.21 in the latest quarter against $0.48 in the year-ago period. Marcus said.
